title: Matrix-Vector Dot Product
prompt: Write a function `matrix_vector_dot(matrix, vector)` that returns the matrix-vector product as a plain Python list. Treat `matrix` as a list of rows and `vector` as a one-dimensional list. A valid input has a non-empty matrix, a non-empty vector, every row non-empty, and every row length equal to `len(vector)`. For valid input, return one dot product per matrix row by summing `row[i] * vector[i]` across all indices. For any invalid shape, return `-1` instead of raising an exception. Invalid shapes include an empty matrix, an empty vector, an empty row, ragged rows, or any row/vector length mismatch. Assume entries are numbers.
